title: Satyajit Ray is one of the greatest Indian filmmakers: Christopher Nolan
summary: Filmmaker Christopher Nolan praised Satyajit Ray's "The Apu Trilogy", calling Ray one of the greatest Indian filmmakers after viewing material at the Criterion Collection in New York. Nolan said he has seen the first film "Pather Panchali" and is eager to watch the remaining two parts. The article also notes the trilogy's awards and Nolan's latest film "The Odyssey", which has earned over $300 million globally.
content:
Published - July 26, 2026 07:06 pm IST - New Delhi

Filmmaker Christopher Nolan praised Satyajit Ray's "The Apu Trilogy" and called him "one of the greatest Indian filmmakers." Nolan visited the Criterion Closet, the famous storage room at the Criterion Collection in New York, where videos circulating online show him admiring Ray's work.

"Then there's 'The Apu Trilogy' by Satyajit Ray, one of the greatest Indian filmmakers. The trilogy starts with 'Pather Panchali', which is an absolutely incredible film. It just blew my mind. I haven't yet seen parts two and three of the trilogy, so I'm pretty excited to get this and complete the story," he is heard saying in the video.

"The Apu Trilogy" comprises three films: "Pather Panchali" (1955), "Aparajito" (1956) and "Apur Sansar" (1959). The series follows the life and journey of Apu from childhood in rural Bengal to adulthood, and is widely regarded as a landmark in Indian and world cinema.

The films received multiple prestigious awards, including the Best Human Document award at Cannes for "Pather Panchali", the Golden Lion at Venice for "Aparajito", and President's Gold Medals at India's National Film Awards.

The article also notes Nolan's recent high-profile project, "The Odyssey", which features an ensemble cast including Matt Damon as Odysseus, Tom Holland as Telemachus, Zendaya as Athena, Robert Pattinson as Antinous, Lupita Nyong'o as Helen of Troy and Clytemnestra, Anne Hathaway as Penelope, and Charlize Theron as Calypso. The film has earned over $300 million at the global box office.

Nolan's comments highlight ongoing international appreciation for Satyajit Ray's work and reflect renewed interest in classic Indian cinema among contemporary filmmakers and cinephiles.
